title: Profit Share Agreement
summary: Give someone a share of a business's or project's net profits without giving them ownership.
useWhen: You want to reward a key contributor, partner or service provider with a share of profits from a business line or project, without issuing equity.
watchOuts: Define 'net profit' precisely: which expenses count, who decides, and whether owner salaries are deducted. Vague definitions cause most profit-share disputes.
If the participant is an employee, profit-share payments are wages and must follow wage-payment and tax-withholding rules.
If the participant pays money for the profit share, it may be an investment contract (a security).
Profit-sharing between licensed professionals and unlicensed persons is prohibited in some fields (law, medicine, real estate).

variables.label: Business owner: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: Participant: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: Profits from
variables.help: The whole business, a product line, a location or a project.

variables.label: Net profit means
variables.default: Gross revenue actually received from the covered business, minus the direct costs of goods and services, operating expenses, reasonable owner compensation, taxes other than income taxes, and debt service, all determined under the owner's consistently applied accounting method.
variables.help: Be specific about included and excluded expenses.

variables.label: Cap total payments?
variables.help: Set a maximum total amount payable.

variables.label: Maximum total payments
variables.help: Total payments will not exceed this.

variables.label: Conditions to stay eligible
variables.default: Participant continues to provide the services described in the parties' services agreement.
variables.help: E.g. continued services. Leave blank for none.

variables.label: Governing law (state)
variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 2. Covered profits
sections.body: This agreement covers net profit from: {{scope}}

sections.title: 3. Profit share
sections.body: For each {{period}} period during the term, Owner will pay Participant {{share_percent}}% of net profit. If net profit for a period is zero or negative, nothing is due for that period, and losses are not carried forward unless both parties agree in writing.

sections.title: 4. Cap
sections.body: Total payments under this agreement will not exceed {{cap}}. Once the cap is reached, Owner's payment obligations end.

sections.title: 6. Statements and audit
sections.body: With each payment, which is due within {{payment_days}} days after each period ends, Owner will provide a statement showing revenue, expenses and the calculation. Once per year, on 30 days' notice, Participant may have an independent accountant review the relevant records at Participant's expense. If the review shows an underpayment of more than 5%, Owner pays for the review and the shortfall.

sections.title: 8. No ownership
sections.body: Participant receives a contractual right to payment only. Participant does not own any part of the business, has no vote or management rights, and is not a partner. Owner runs the business in its reasonable discretion but will not take actions intended to avoid profit-share payments.

sections.title: 9. Term and ending
sections.body: This agreement lasts {{term_months}} months from {{effective_date}}. Amounts earned for periods before it ends are still payable. If the covered business is sold, Owner will pay the profit share through the closing date.

sections.title: 10. Taxes
sections.body: Each party is responsible for its own taxes. Owner will issue required tax forms.

sections.title: 11. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Owner** — {{owner_name}}

[[sig:owner]]

Printed name: [[name:owner]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:owner:Title]]
Date: [[date:owner]]

**Participant** — {{participant_name}}

[[sig:participant]]

Printed name: [[name:participant]]
Date: [[date:participant]]
